ch000.alt: A brick archway spanning a Shanghai lane, three roundels on it reading Ping'an Li, opening on a narrow stone-paved alley lined with old shikumen houses.
ch000.caption: Old shikumen lane-houses of Shanghai. (The 2019 reprint's caption; a photograph added by its editor, not a figure of the 1933 book.)

ch001.alt: A man on a doorstep pressing a diamond-set fortune character and red paper couplets onto a weathered wooden door.
ch001.caption: Pasting up spring couplets. (The 2019 reprint's caption; a photograph added by its editor, not a figure of the 1933 book.)

ch001.before: The lazy streak in the Chinese
ch001.alt: An ink line-drawing of a woman in an apron reaching up with a long feather-duster to sweep the eaves of a shopfront while a child looks on; a cartouche reads Sweeping the Eaves-Dust.
ch001.caption: The year-end cleaning. (The 2019 reprint's caption, given to a period line-drawing titled "Sweeping the Eaves-Dust" that its editor added; not a figure of the 1933 book.)

ch001.before: Through the first days of the New Year, men and women
ch001.alt: A laughing little girl in a red brocade jacket holding a candied-hawthorn stick and red envelopes beside a door bearing the character for spring.
ch001.caption: In new clothes. (The 2019 reprint's caption; a photograph added by its editor, not a figure of the 1933 book.)

ch001.before: Close the shop and you let off
ch001.alt: Fireworks and firecrackers throwing up sprays of sparks in a dark courtyard, with two figures silhouetted against the glare.
ch001.caption: Setting off firecrackers. (The 2019 reprint's caption; a photograph added by its editor, not a figure of the 1933 book.)

ch002.alt: A studio portrait of a clean-shaven young man in a high-collared Western coat and tie, hair swept back.
ch002.caption: Song Jiaoren. (Reprint caption: 'Song Jiaoren'. A photograph added by the 2019 editor, not a figure of the 1933 book.)

ch002.before: everyone knows them for Zhao Bingjun
ch002.alt: A studio portrait of a mustached man in an embroidered silk mandarin gown with a round dragon roundel.
ch002.caption: Ying Guixin, the go-between in the plot. (Reprint caption: 'Ying Guixin'. A photograph added by the 2019 editor, not a figure of the 1933 book.)

ch002.before: Earlier, after Mr. Song had declined
ch002.alt: A drawn portrait of a balding man in wire-rimmed spectacles, wing collar and cravat.
ch002.caption: Hong Shuzu, who relayed the orders. (Reprint caption: 'Hong Shuzu'. An image added by the 2019 editor, not a figure of the 1933 book.)

ch002.alt: A studio portrait of a heavyset man with a small mustache in a dark Chinese gown, a landscape backdrop behind.
ch002.caption: Zhao Bingjun, Yuan's premier and the case's named principal. (Reprint caption: 'Zhao Bingjun'. A photograph added by the 2019 editor, not a figure of the 1933 book.)

ch003.before: Mr. Dai Jitao, President of the Examination Yuan
ch003.alt: A studio portrait of a man with a small mustache in a pale high-collared Chinese jacket.
ch003.caption: Dai Jitao. (Reprint caption: 'Dai Jitao'. A photograph added by the 2019 editor, not a figure of the 1933 book.)

ch005.before: Cai Yuanpei, Wu Zhihui, Zhang Taiyan
ch005.alt: A portrait of a broad-faced man with short hair and a level gaze, in a dark collared jacket.
ch005.caption: Zhang Taiyan. (Reprint caption: 'Zhang Taiyan'. A photograph added by the 2019 editor, not a figure of the 1933 book.)

ch006.before: In the Wuxu coup at the close
ch006.alt: A full-length studio portrait of a bearded elderly man in a silk gown, standing before a flowered backdrop.
ch006.caption: Kang Youwei. (Reprint caption: 'Kang Youwei'. A photograph added by the 2019 editor, not a figure of the 1933 book.)

ch010.alt: A magazine cover, a line drawing of a bobbed-haired young woman resting her chin on her hand over a closed book, lettered 'The Saturday, No. 122'.
ch010.caption: A cover of the fiction weekly Libai Liu (The Saturday). (Reprint illustration added by the 2019 editor, not a figure of the 1933 book.)

ch010.before: Speaking of all these many magazines
ch010.alt: The front page of a tabloid-format weekly with the masthead character-title 'Shenghuo' set in a decorative border.
ch010.caption: Zou Taofen's Shenghuo (Life) Weekly. (Reprint illustration added by the 2019 editor, not a figure of the 1933 book.)

ch010.before: As for how often they come out
ch010.alt: A magazine cover with a bold title 'Shiritan' above a crowded allegorical drawing, lettered 'Decameron No. 35'.
ch010.caption: Shao Xunmei's Shiritan (Decameron). (Reprint illustration added by the 2019 editor, not a figure of the 1933 book.)

ch012.before: The middle stretch of Fuzhou Road
ch012.alt: A street photograph of a busy multi-story corner building with shop signboards and pedestrians, in old Shanghai.
ch012.caption: Bookshops on Fuzhou Road, old Shanghai. (Reprint caption: 'Old Shanghai, Fuzhou Road bookshops'. A photograph added by the 2019 editor, not a figure of the 1933 book.)

ch013.before: The new drama (that is, spoken drama
ch013.alt: An ink cartoon of a knot of young men before a large painted playbill that shows two faces and reads, in Chinese and Japanese, 'Chunliu Society' and 'Camille'.
ch013.caption: A cartoon of the Chunliu Society's benefit performance in Japan (the playbill names Camille). (Reprint caption: 'A cartoon concerning the Chunliu Society's charity performance in Japan'. Added by the 2019 editor, not a figure of the 1933 book.)

ch013.alt: A studio portrait of a man in round spectacles and a Chinese gown, hair brushed back.
ch013.caption: Zheng Zhengqiu. (Reprint caption: 'Zheng Zhengqiu'. A photograph added by the 2019 editor, not a figure of the 1933 book.)

ch037.alt: An old black-and-white photograph of a bearded fortune-teller seated behind a cloth-draped table on a Shanghai street; the cloth bears columns of white characters and a large yin-yang and eight-trigrams emblem, with a teapot and cups on the table.
ch037.caption: A character-splitting stall in old Shanghai. (The 2019 reprint's caption; a photograph added by its editor, not a figure of the 1933 book.)

ch052.before: Zhang's Garden, otherwise called the Weiyuan
ch052.alt: An old black-and-white photograph of a tall Western-style mansion with a campanile tower rising above a lush garden of willows and shrubs; this is Arcadia Hall in Zhang's Garden.
ch052.caption: The Weiyuan (Zhang's Garden), with Arcadia Hall rising behind the trees. (The 2019 reprint's caption; a photograph added by its editor, not a figure of the 1933 book.)

ch053.before: The late Huang Chujiu was the founding father
ch053.alt: A studio portrait of a middle-aged man in a round satin cap and a dark embroidered silk gown, seated and facing the camera.
ch053.caption: Huang Chujiu. (Reprint caption: 'Huang Chujiu'. A photograph added by the 2019 editor, not a figure of the 1933 book.)

ch056.before: In the opening years of the Xianfeng reign
ch056.alt: An aerial photograph looking down the Bund: in the foreground the steel-truss Garden Bridge crosses the mouth of Suzhou Creek, with the lawns of the Public Garden beside it; the Huangpu beyond is crowded with junks and steam launches, and the tall buildings of the Bund line the right-hand shore.
ch056.caption: The Garden Bridge and the Bund, Shanghai, from above. (Reprint caption: 'Garden Bridge on the Bund, Shanghai'. A photograph added by the 2019 editor, not a figure of the 1933 book.)

ch063.before: The tiger stove is a little shop
ch063.alt: A woman at a tiled tiger-stove counter fills a customer's tall enamel thermos flask from a boiler; a queue of people wait behind her, each holding a vacuum flask.
ch063.caption: A tiger stove supplying hot water, its customers filling their flasks. (Reprint caption: 'A tiger stove, for hot water only'. A later documentary photograph added by the 2019 editor, not a figure of the 1933 book.)

ch072.before: Not long ago old Mr. Wu Zhihui
ch072.alt: A studio portrait of an elderly man with a bald crown, a wispy white moustache and goatee, in a dark Chinese gown, smiling faintly.
ch072.caption: Wu Zhihui. (A portrait added by the 2019 editor; the label is the reprint's.)

ch072.before: Not long ago old Mr. Wu Zhihui
ch072.alt: A studio portrait of a stern middle-aged man with a shaved head and heavy brows, in a dark Chinese gown.
ch072.caption: Rong Zongjing. (A portrait added by the 2019 editor; the label is the reprint's.)

ch088.before: In former days both Sheng Xingsun
ch088.alt: A painted portrait of an elderly Qing official in a round black cap and dark gown, with a thin grey beard.
ch088.caption: Sheng Xuanhuai (courtesy name Xingsun). (A portrait added by the 2019 editor; the label is the reprint's.)

ch088.before: In former days both Sheng Xingsun
ch088.alt: A hillside grave: a tall black headstone carved 'Tomb of Mr. Zhu Baosan' beside a low stone wall with an inscribed tablet and a stone bench.
ch088.caption: The tomb of Zhu Baosan. (A photograph added by the 2019 editor; the label is the reprint's.)

ch088.before: In former days both Sheng Xingsun
ch088.alt: A night street scene: foreign military police and sailors standing beside a bilingual street sign reading RUE CHU-PAO-SAN and, in Chinese, Zhu Baosan Road.
ch088.caption: Rue Chu-Pao-San, the French Concession street named for Zhu Baosan. (A photograph added by the 2019 editor; the label is the reprint's.)

ch096.before: There are two kinds of carrying-pole
ch096.alt: A brush cartoon of a wonton peddler bending under a shoulder-pole, a low stove and basket slung at one end and a cabinet of little drawers at the other.
ch096.caption: The Wonton Carrying-Pole, a brush cartoon by the artist Feng Zikai (1898–1975), signed with his studio-name and his mark ‘TK.’ (An illustration added by the 2019 editor; not a figure of the 1933 book.)

ch098.before: For the people who live in Shanghai
ch098.alt: A tailor sits working at a cloth-covered table against a brick wall; a tall hanging banner beside him is lettered as a Su-Guang ready-made clothier.
ch098.caption: A Su-Guang ready-made clothier’s street pitch, the banner reading ‘Zhang’s Su-Guang Ready-Made Clothier.’ (A photograph added by the 2019 editor; the label is the reprint’s.)

ch099.alt: A crowded temple courtyard where buyers in winter coats bend over long tables heaped with secondhand books.
ch099.caption: The secondhand-book market in the courtyard of the City God Temple, a recent photograph. (Added by the 2019 editor; not a figure of the 1933 book.)

ch100.before: The third-floor boxes of a theater
ch100.alt: The interior of a traditional Chinese theater: tiers of carved wooden balcony boxes above rows of stalls seating.
ch100.caption: The boxes of a traditional theater. (A photograph added by the 2019 editor; the label is the reprint’s.)
